title: Lusha Pricing: Plans, Credits & Costs in 2026
summary: Lusha pricing shows all five tiers with credit costs and monthly fees. Compare plan features to pick the right fit for your team's prospecting budget.
body_markdown:
## Fixing the Lusha-to-CRM handoff with Activepieces


If you want to stop paying twice for the same contact, Activepieces, an MIT-licensed automation platform with 744 integrations, can do it, but it can't make a contact reachable. It supplies no contact data of its own.


What it does is sit between your leads and Lusha and make sure every credit you spend lands somewhere your team will use it.


It targets plain waste. When a rep reveals someone a colleague already revealed last month, **the credit's gone for nothing** .


Or a rep reveals a number, copies it into a notes file, and it never reaches the customer record, so nobody calls. Both inflate the cost per reached contact, the figure that matters, without showing up on any invoice.


One caution before you build anything: check that your Lusha plan includes API access, and look for a Lusha integration among the 744 integrations in the Activepieces open source monorepo, before you code it yourself, since without one the workflow has to call Lusha's API directly.


Some plans gate this, and if yours does, the fix costs more than the leak.


A workflow that checks the CRM, asks Lusha, writes back and posts to Slack is several steps, but the pricing page at activepieces.com/pricing sets a flow run at 1 credit, any number of steps.


Putting the duplicate check in its own step to protect your Lusha credits adds nothing to that bill, whereas the pricing pages of Zapier and Make show per-task billing at the one and per-module billing at the other, so each step is charged.


The free plan carries 1,000 of those credits a month with unlimited flows, so the whole handoff can be tried before anyone approves a budget.


### Check the CRM before spending a credit


When a new lead arrives, the workflow's first step looks the lead up in your CRM, the system where customer records live. If a record already holds a phone number and email, the workflow stops and spends nothing.


Only when the lookup comes back empty does it ask Lusha for a reveal.


That one branch is the whole saving. You're no longer relying on each rep to remember who was already looked up.


### Write enriched data back and flag low credits


After a reveal, the workflow writes the result straight onto the CRM record. The next person who opens that lead sees the data, and the next lookup finds it, so the same contact is never bought twice.


Last, the workflow watches your remaining balance. When credits run low, a message goes to a Slack channel your team already reads. That turns a surprise, reps hitting an empty balance mid-week, into a warning with time to act.


Take from it that the paid step sits behind a free check, and nothing is revealed without being saved.


Once it's running, the figure from the previous section becomes easier to trust, because duplicate reveals and lost results no longer pad the denominator.
